newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WINS RACE, GERG GRABS SUPER-G TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WINS RACE, GERG GRABS SUPER-G TITLE.

text.p: German great Katja Seizinger won the battle but compatriot Hilde Gerg won the war Thursday as she snatched the women's Super-G season title by finishing second in a German medals sweep at the World Cup Finals.

Seizinger, second by a scant three-hundredths of a second in Wednesday's downhill, bounced back to triumph with a sizzling run through a tricky, 34-gate course that claimed several casualties among the star-studded field.
But the 24-year-old Seizinger was deprived of the season's title by the second-place finish of Gerg, who won the crown by 16 points with a 490 total.
"This season was absolutely beyond my wildest dreams," said the 21-year-old Gerg, who captured world championship bronze in the Super-G and combined at Sestriere.
Seizinger, winner of 27 World Cup races, sliced through the fast course in a time of one minute, 15.73 seconds.
"I had a perfect run today," said Seizinger, who was head and shoulders better than the field Thursday.

Gerg, skiing right after Seizinger from the 15th position, was a full eight-tenths of a second slower at 1:16.53. But her second-place time held up and that was enough to push her past Seizinger for the Super-G title.
Germany's Martina Ertl claimed third place in 1:17.01, six-hundredths of a second ahead of Ingeborg Helen Marken of Norway.

Overall World Cup champion Pernilla Wiberg entered the race with a 39-point lead in the Super-G standings. But the Swede, who won her first career downhill here Wednesday, skied out on the same blind turn that claimed Swiss star Heidi Zurbriggen and Italian Isolde Kostner, who entered the race with a mathematical chance for the season title.
Wiberg settled for third in the Super-G title hunt on 449 points.
Women's downhill champion Renate Goetschl of Austria also failed to finish the course after Gerg had posted her time.
"It was very dramatic as I had to wait at the finish line and very nerve wracking," said Gerg.
"My fate was in somebody else's hands. It's tough being totally dependent on others," added Gerg, who who also won a Super-G this season at Val d'Isere.

Seizinger, who said she had lost eight or nine races by narrow margins this season, lamented another close call against her but said she had not built her hopes too high for claiming the Super-G crown.
"I had just a little chance to win," she of her title chances. "But it was great to win the race after not winning the downhill yesterday."
